messages.content: I have the two hotel screens open. The Palmer House two-queen rate shows $1,389.20 for four nights, but I can now see a $25 nightly urban destination charge in the details. The Hampton Majestic king study is showing $1,312.84 with breakfast, but the search result says two guests. Can you verify what we would actually pay for three people and which room gives our daughter a real bed?

Yes. I’ll separate the room charges, taxes, and mandatory fees, then confirm whether the Hampton room permits three registered guests and whether its sofa converts to a bed. I’ll also compare the cancellation deadlines before recommending one.
The dates are June 25 through June 29, four nights. She’s 14, so I don’t want to assume the hotel treats her as a small child who can share our bed.

Understood. The Palmer House listing confirms a maximum occupancy of four in the two-queen room, so all three of you can be registered without an additional-person charge. Its $1,389.20 display already includes $1,096.00 in room charges, $193.20 in taxes, and the mandatory $100 urban destination charge for four nights. The two queen beds are the only sleeping surfaces needed.
Good. What did you find on the Hampton? The room name on my screen just says one king study.

The full room description identifies one king bed plus a full-size pullout sofa. The hotel has confirmed that the room’s maximum occupancy is three and that a 14-year-old can be added as the third registered guest at no extra charge. The sofa bed is included; a rollaway is neither needed nor permitted in that room.
Does adding her change the $1,312.84 total? Please make sure breakfast isn’t a separate package charge.

No. Repricing the same refundable king-study rate for two adults and one 14-year-old keeps the four-night total at $1,312.84: $1,116.00 for the room and $196.84 in taxes. There is no destination or urban fee. Breakfast for all three registered guests is complimentary rather than a paid package, and Wi-Fi is also included.
So the Hampton is $76.36 less, correct? What are we giving up besides having the sofa bed instead of a second queen?

Correct: $1,389.20 minus $1,312.84 is $76.36. The main tradeoff is the sleeping setup. The Palmer gives you two permanent queen beds, while the Hampton requires opening the full-size sofa each night. Both are in the Loop and workable for the theater and Art Institute. The Hampton includes breakfast; the Palmer’s mandatory charge includes property credits, but breakfast is not automatically included.
Compare the cancellation language. The Palmer page says June 21, but I need the actual cutoff times.

The Palmer rate can be canceled without penalty through 11:59 p.m. Central on June 21; after that, the penalty is one night plus tax. The Hampton rate can be canceled without penalty until 6:00 p.m. Central on June 23; after that, one night plus tax is charged. Neither option requires a nonrefundable prepayment tonight, although each hotel may place a temporary card authorization.
The sofa bed is acceptable for this trip if it is definitely part of the room and she is on the reservation. Choose between them and update the overall trip number from the $3,750.20 estimate.

Choose the Hampton Majestic king-study room for three registered guests at the mandatory four-night total of $1,312.84. The confirmed full-size pullout sofa gives your daughter a designated sleeping surface, breakfast is included for all three, and the cancellation window remains open two days longer. Replacing the $1,389.20 Palmer amount lowers the complete trip estimate by $76.36, from $3,750.20 to $3,673.84, leaving $326.16 under the $4,000 ceiling.
All right. Give me the final order for tonight so I can release the theater hold without losing it.

Book the refundable Hampton Majestic king-study rate first, with two adults and one 14-year-old listed, and confirm the payment page still shows one king bed plus a full-size sofa bed, complimentary breakfast for three, no mandatory property fee, a $1,312.84 total, and free cancellation until 6:00 p.m. Central on June 23. Once the hotel confirmation reflects all three guests and that room type, accept the $354 Saturday matinee hold before it expires tomorrow evening. Then purchase the verified Love Field–Midway nonstop flights. The planning total for flights, hotel, theater, museums, transportation, and meals is $3,673.84.
